description: Figure 5 is described by its caption as a two-panel figure ("(b) Fig. 5") of carbon-concentration maps obtained by atom-probe tomography (APT) — not EDS — for (a) 0.006%P and (b) 0.043%P steels aged 10 h at 530°C; however, the supplied crop contains only ONE map, and the panel itself carries no visible (a)/(b) letter. That single panel is a smooth, colour-coded square field whose four sides are ticked −30, −20, −10, 0, 10, 20, 30 with no axis titles printed; the nanometre unit comes only from the caption, so the field spans roughly 65 × 65 nm. The colour ramp runs blue (carbon-poor) to red (carbon-rich); the caption states the scale is 2–6 at.% C, but no colour bar is rendered in the crop, so that range cannot be verified from the pixels. The field displays a modulated, spinodal-type microstructure: interconnected elongated red/orange carbon-rich domains, a few nanometres to roughly 15 nm long judging from the tick spacing, separated by irregular blue carbon-poor channels with diffuse, non-faceted boundaries. The figure's argument, completed by the missing (a) panel, is that ageing at 530°C produces fine-scale spinodal decomposition whose amplitude/wavelength depends on phosphorus content.

observations.observation: The supplied image is a single square 2-D colour-coded field-map with both axes ticked −30, −20, −10, 0, 10, 20, 30 and no axis titles printed anywhere in the panel.
No colour bar or numeric composition legend is rendered inside the supplied panel, so the 2–6 at.% C blue-to-red scale cannot be confirmed from the pixels.

The map shows a modulated microstructure of elongated, interconnected red/orange high-carbon domains (a few nanometres up to roughly 15 nm long against the axis ticks) separated by irregular blue low-carbon channels with diffuse boundaries.
The supplied crop contains only one map; the second map described by the caption is absent, and neither map carries a visible (a)/(b) panel letter in the pixels.
The caption states the maps are carbon concentration maps (2–6 at.% C, blue to red) obtained from APT analysis.
The caption states the maps compare (a) 0.006%P and (b) 0.043%P steels aged for 10 h at 530°C and show the progress of spinodal decomposition.
The caption gives the spatial scale of the maps in nanometres; the printed tick values (−30 to 30, step 10) therefore correspond to a field of roughly 65 × 65 nm.
The citing text asserts that phosphorus greatly increases the rate of spinodal decomposition during ageing at 530°C, as shown in Fig. 5.
The citing text states that phosphorus was found to be randomly distributed between the matrix and the κ-carbide, so the increased hardening rate is not related to long-range diffusion of phosphorus.

The citing text reports that the compared steels are Fe-30Mn-9Al-1Si-0.9C-0.5Mo (also referred to for the 0.001%P and 0.043%P conditions), placing Fig. 5 in a high-Mn, high-Al lightweight-steel context.
